text: Per-grob title and description added in 22656c4. Grob.annotated(child, GrobMeta) attaches an optional title and description (plus a CssClass and DataKey pairs, see intaglio-paint-class) to any grob. Grob.Annotated has no viewport and no name of its own, so name collection and depth-first traversal are unchanged; device lowering delegates to the child and records the metadata as DeviceElement.Annotated, which the SVG backend emits as a wrapping <g> whose first children are <title> and <desc>. Canvas, Java2D, JavaFX and PDF draw the child as if the wrapper were absent, and RendererConformance gains an 'annotated' case so every backend harness proves acceptance and transparency. Acceptance met: a named grob with a title renders <g ...><title>...</title><circle data-name=...>...</g>; a grob without a title renders byte-identically to before, pinned by SvgAnnotationSuite's FNV-1a digest of all 41 pre-annotation conformance cases at 240x160; escaping of <, & and ]]> is asserted, as is supplementary-plane text; the suite runs on JVM and Scala.js so those exact strings are also determinism checks; XML-illegal characters are a typed SvgRenderError naming the field. storyatlas4s confirmed VoyageLowering can set a unit's words as the title and that data-name on the child still resolves through closest('[data-name]'). Documented in docs/accessibility.md. Not established: metadata reaches no backend but SVG; raster hit-testing does not expose it. Recorded in CHANGELOG.md at storyatlas4s's request: titles are validated for XML code points only, so a caller feeding human text should strip control characters itself rather than treat that check as sanitisation.
